notes: This page opens section 4, Sections d’extensions, et anneaux de valuation généraux, and establishes notation for outer and chosen profinite fundamental groups, then the affine-ring and geometric-point versions. It ends mid-sentence at Le choix; nothing is completed.

Line count 23 under the root all-ink logical-line convention: 19 main text/display/heading baselines, 2 supralinear insertions, and 2 standalone numbering entries (top 52 and lower-left 104). The spatially separate page number 52 is counted independently even though its y-position is near the title insertion. Formula (3) and the prose beginning où share main line 18; formula and section numbers are already included in main lines.

The source says rev. universel profini de E_X at line 7. That is the symbol in the ink, although the surrounding discussion would naturally suggest a covering of X. Both witnesses agree, and it is not silently corrected.

The page contains no genuine diagram or drawing. The large curved strokes at the title and above line 12 are insertion leaders, not parentheses or pictures. The line under the heading is a continuous underline.

The crossing-out before note is restricted to the prefix, with a separate crossed-out E_X after note. The doubtful prefix dé is present in C.tex but is not an id in marks.tsv. Following root instruction, it is recorded in doubts and the deletion change only, without inventing a mark id.
The six point-letter occurrences have the same reduced form. Zeta is put first on visual grounds; xi remains a real alternative. No external convention or other page has been used to settle it.
Lower-left 104 is in thinner, smaller writing than the principal text and is treated as foliation; it is not identified as the author’s page number. The authorial page number at top is 52.

Crop p06 was inspected but its upper bound clipped part of the still-unsettled tiny insertion. Before any decision on M0006, p16 was made with the needed upper context and inspected. p16 is the authoritative evidence crop for that region; no decided place was recropped.

The isolated faint trace between algèbre and telle is substantially lighter than the foreground lettering and has no secure textual reading; it is treated as show-through or paper trace rather than inserted words.
No mathematical proof appears on this page. The work here is paleographical transcription and local notation comparison, not an independent proof verification.
